outcome.answer:
Several papers address robust intent classification for chatbots. The closest match is a systematic evaluation of open-weight intent classifiers that studies robustness to realistic input perturbations, calibration, deployment efficiency, and model ranking stability across multiple intent datasets [1]. Another paper focuses specifically on noise-robust conversational intent classification and finds that attention pooling is better under noisy conditions, while mean pooling can hurt performance [2]. A third study reports that training-based classifiers are better on harder intent tasks, while training-free methods are generally more robust to mixed-intent and adversarial prompts [3].

For broader chatbot settings, one paper proposes an open-intent method with stronger detection of unknown intents and improved open-world robustness [4], and another builds uncertainty estimation for open-set text classification, including intent datasets, to predict when a system will make recognition errors [10].
